literal: Than the highly intimate friendship of a fool, the estrangement of those who have wisdom is ten million times better.
translation: Rather than the highly intimate friendship of a fool, the complete estrangement of wise people is ten million times better.
modern: ஒரு பேதையின் மிக நெருக்கமான நட்பை விட, அறிவுடையவர்களின் பகைமை அல்லது விலகியிருக்கும் தன்மை கோடி மடங்கு மேலானதாகும்.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the close friendship of an ignorant person with the complete estrangement of wise people. The word 'பேதை' refers to a fool whose intense intimacy ('பெருங்கெழீஇ நட்பு') is unstable and dangerous. On the other hand, 'ஏதின்மை' refers to being strangers or having no relationship. The poet asserts that having no connection with wise people ('அறிவுடையார்') is ten million ('கோடி') times better ('உறும்') than being close to a fool, because even the indifference of the wise does no harm, whereas the friendship of a fool is inherently ruinous.
